title: Music Collaboration Agreement
summary: Two artists or producers making a joint project agree on ownership of songs and masters, costs, decisions, income and credit.
useWhen: Two creators are working on a joint single, EP or album that neither will own alone.
watchOuts: Every recorded song has two separate copyrights: the composition (music and lyrics), usually owned by songwriters and their publishers, and the sound recording or master, usually owned by whoever paid for or made the recording (the artist or label). Licenses and splits for one do not cover the other. Agree on both.

Under U.S. law, each co-owner of a joint work can usually grant non-exclusive licenses without the others' consent, but must share profits. This agreement adds consent requirements so one collaborator can't license the project alone.
If either collaborator is signed to a label or publisher, their deal may claim their share. Check exclusivity clauses and get waivers.
Decide what happens to unreleased material if the collaboration ends.

sections.title: 1. Parties and project
sections.body:
**Collaborator A:** {{collab_a_name}}, {{collab_a_address}} ({{collab_a_email}})

**Collaborator B:** {{collab_b_name}}, {{collab_b_address}} ({{collab_b_email}})

The collaborators will create {{project}} (the "Project"), starting {{effective_date}}.

sections.title: 2. Compositions
sections.body: Each song's composition will be owned by its writers in the shares recorded in a split sheet signed on the day the song is written, or as soon as possible after. No song will be released without a signed split sheet.

sections.title: 3. Masters
sections.body: The Project's master recordings are owned: Collaborator A {{master_split_a}}%, Collaborator B {{master_split_b}}%. Master income is shared in the same proportions, after recording costs are recouped as agreed.

sections.title: 4. Costs
sections.body: Recording, mixing, mastering, artwork and video costs are paid {{costs}}. Budget: {{budget}}. Neither collaborator will spend more than $500 on the Project without the other's written approval.

sections.title: 5. Releases and decisions
sections.body: Release dates, the tracklist, artwork, distributor, pricing and marketing require both collaborators' approval. Distribution: {{distributor}}. Credit: {{credit_format}}.

sections.title: 6. Licensing
sections.body: Neither collaborator will license the Project's masters or compositions they co-own, including for sync, sampling or remixes, without the other's written approval, which will not be unreasonably withheld for customary non-exclusive licenses at market rates. Each will promptly share all license offers.

sections.title: 7. Income and accounting
sections.body: Where the distributor or society can split income at source, the collaborators will set up splits there. Otherwise, the collaborator who receives income will account to the other within 30 days after the end of each quarter, with statements, and pay the other's share.

sections.title: 8. Name and likeness
sections.body: Each collaborator may use the other's approved name, likeness and biography to promote the Project.

sections.title: 9. Leaving the collaboration
sections.body: Either collaborator may end the collaboration for future work with 30 days' written notice. Released material stays co-owned and administered under this agreement. Unreleased material may be released only with both collaborators' consent. Neither may use the other's unreleased contributions in other projects without consent.

sections.title: 10. Promises
sections.body: Each collaborator's contributions are original or cleared, and they are free to enter this agreement, or have obtained any needed label or publisher waiver.

sections.title: 11. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Collaborator A** — {{collab_a_name}}

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Music rights are split between the composition (song) and the sound recording (master); royalties also depend on PRO, publisher, distributor and label agreements that this template does not change. An entertainment attorney should review deals involving advances, ownership transfers or long terms.
